claims.claim: ICoinLedger.MergeFrom(IEnumerable<Op>) EXISTS at pin 02bcc20: it is declared on the ICoinLedger interface and is implemented (not stubbed, not NotImplementedException) by CoinProvenanceStore as a single-expression delegation to the op-WAL.

claims.claim: CoinProvenanceStore.MergeFrom performs ZERO validation of peer ops: it contains no op-type check, no conservation check, no witness-certificate verification and no call into CommutativeOpProcessor.Validate — the whole method body is `_wal.Merge(ops)`.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/Provenance/CoinProvenanceStore.cs:104 — full method body is `=> _wal.Merge(ops);` with no other statements

claims.claim: Folding peer coin ops via MergeFrom structurally BYPASSES the seam where the coin ledger enforces its spend invariant: CoinProvenanceStore.Append throws InvalidOperationException for a Spend op so that only the E3PC gate's AppendCommittedSpend may admit one, but MergeFrom writes to the same WAL with no such guard, so a peer-supplied Spend op reaches the WAL without passing any local gate.

claims.claim: MergeFrom does not update any in-memory balance projection — it only writes the WAL — so after an anti-entropy merge a live CommutativeOpProcessor instance is stale until a fresh processor rehydrates from the WAL.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/Provenance/CoinProvenanceStore.cs:104 (no Project call); corroborated by the shipped test Olamnit/Olamnit.Coin.Tests/Ledger/Commutative/CommutativeOpProcessorTests.cs:163-174 which, after `storeB.MergeFrom(...)`, constructs FRESH processors (`new CommutativeOpProcessor(new CoinProvenanceStore(dbA, "peer-a"))`) to observe merged balances rather than reading procA/procB

claims.claim: The missing re-validation on the peer-merge path is a KNOWN, code-documented, deliberately out-of-v1-scope gap (labelled 'CROSS-HOST FOLLOW-UP (codexreview, out of v1 scope — OE-4)'), not an undiscovered defect: the comment states rehydration Projects every WAL op WITHOUT re-running admission checks or witness-cert verification, and that once MergeFrom folds peer ops both rehydration and MergeFrom must re-validate before projecting.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/Commutative/CommutativeOpProcessor.cs:60-65

claims.claim: CommutativeOpProcessor rehydration is the actual projection path for merged peer ops and it calls Project(envelope) directly in the constructor with NO Validate call, so any op that reached the WAL via MergeFrom is projected into balances unvalidated on the next restart or audit replay.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/Commutative/CommutativeOpProcessor.cs:57-59 (`foreach (var (_, envelope) in ledger.OpsIn(CoinBoxes.Ledger)) Project(envelope);`)

claims.claim: A naive 'validate every op before projecting' fix to the merge path would BREAK convergence rather than fix it, because CommutativeOpProcessor.Validate is order-dependent: it returns RejectedUnknownRef for any split/merge/charge/aging whose referenced mint or leaf is not yet in the local projection, so a peer delta replayed in a non-causal order would reject legitimate ops. Correct re-validation-before-projection therefore requires causal/dependency ordering of the merged op set, not merely calling Validate.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/Commutative/CommutativeOpProcessor.cs:173-182 (Validate dispatch), :176 (ChargeBody => RejectedUnknownRef when `!_dags.ContainsKey`), :201-202 and :227-228 (RejectedUnknownRef on unseen leaf), :267-268 (aging RejectedUnknownRef); Op.Create carries `deps` at CoinProvenanceStore.cs:82 but Validate never consults them

claims.claim: Correct re-validation-before-projection additionally requires changing CommutativeOpProcessor.Validate, because today Validate maps SpendBody to RejectedMalformed unconditionally, which means the public Replay path rejects EVERY committed spend already in the WAL — the code comment names this as a required change so 'the recovery paths agree'.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/Commutative/CommutativeOpProcessor.cs:180 (`SpendBody => OpAdmission.RejectedMalformed`), :107-117 (Replay calls Validate), :64-65 (comment: 'Replay must accept a committed SpendBody (today it returns RejectedMalformed)')

claims.claim: The coin ledger NEVER verifies the WitnessCert on a mint op: CommutativeOpProcessor.ValidateMint checks only non-zero value, non-empty provider, mint-id novelty, the funding split sum, and the pool bound — no signature check. A repository-wide grep of Olamnit.Coin/Ledger for Ed25519/Verify shows witness-certificate verification occurring ONLY on the spend path (SpendGate). Mint authorization is therefore enforced entirely outside the ledger engine.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/Commutative/CommutativeOpProcessor.cs:184-195 (ValidateMint body, no cert check); grep 'Ed25519|Verify|WitnessCert' over Olamnit/Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/ → only Olamnit/Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/Settlement/SpendGate.cs:139 (`_certVerifier.Verify(cert, _quorum.WitnessCount)`) verifies a cert

claims.claim: The design's stated conviction mechanism for a forged merged mint — the pool audit — does NOT detect supply inflation. PoolAudit checks `circulating + pool == fresh`; a forged mint with FundingFreshUCoin = V adds V to `fresh` AND V to `circulating` (a new live DAG root), so the identity still holds and the audit returns Holds=true. PoolAudit only convicts a pool OVERDRAW (poolOut > poolIn) and DAG-internal conservation breaks.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/Validity/PoolAudit.cs:41-62 (`fresh += mint.FundingFreshUCoin`, `circulating = replay.TotalCirculating()`, `holds = circulating + pool == fresh && replay.VerifyAllConservation()`), :55-58 (the only overdraw refusal); INFERENCE from the arithmetic as read, not from an executed test

claims.claim: CommutativeOpProcessor.Project deliberately CLAMPS a forged pool overdraw to zero instead of throwing, with an in-code comment naming the pool audit as the mechanism that 'convicts it' — so the engine's designed answer to a hostile merged mint is a later audit, not admission-time refusal.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/Commutative/CommutativeOpProcessor.cs:289-293 (`// pool-first drawdown (FR-010a) — Admit validated ≤ pool; replay of a FORGED overdraw clamps instead of crashing (the pool audit is what convicts it)`)

claims.claim: The auto-endorser's key is derived from the SAME per-host secret as the host itself, merely domain-separated, so the string-equality independence check in EndorseAsync can never fire on the auto path by construction: EndorserKey hashes 'olamnit-rewards-{role}-v1:' with HostIdentity.Seed to produce a key id that structurally cannot equal a wallet id. Auto-endorsement 'independence' at the pin is key-material domain separation on ONE host, not a separate trust domain.

claims.claim: The only real anti-self-attestation strength in the shipped auto-endorsement path is ICorroborationSource, and BOTH shipped implementations reduce to a set-membership lookup (`live.Contains(signal.SourceNativeId)`) against an INJECTED Func<CancellationToken, Task<IReadOnlySet<string>>> — neither verifies any signature. 'Evidence the claimant cannot forge' is therefore only as strong as the independence of whatever function the host injects.

claims.claim: A 1-µcoin-per-hop reward is mintable but is UNSPLITTABLE and UNMERGEABLE dust that can never be aggregated: MicroCoin.TryFloorSplit returns false when the value is below k, and CommutativeOpProcessor.ValidateMerge returns RejectedMalformed for parents spanning different mint DAGs — since each hop reward is its own mint with its own DAG, 1M hop rewards can never be merged into a single balance leaf.

claims.claim: One reward hop costs roughly 20-25 sequential PGlite round trips through RewardsIngestionLoop.ProcessAsync (admission SELECT+INSERT, claim GET, policy version + rules SELECT, binding SELECT, claim INSERT, claim re-GET, endorsement signal SELECT, endorsement existence SELECT + INSERT + UPDATE, mint claim GET, endorsement SELECT, provenance INSERT, signal SELECT, claim close UPDATE), which at 1M hops implies on the order of 2x10^7 round trips — a throughput ceiling in the reward pipeline itself, independent of any link or fsync cost.

claims.claim: Auto-endorsable reward claims expire after 24 hours by default (AutoClaimExpiry / the seeded auto classes' EndorsementWindow), and a periodic ExpirySweep closes any still-awaiting claim as `expired_unendorsed`, so any ring-soak hop whose corroboration is delayed past its window is terminally closed and never mints — a partition longer than the window silently converts hop rewards into expired dispositions.
